solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Penny looks and wrestles with God

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for a penny
Chambers gives ray as a look or glance

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a coin and grapples with the Almighty, as if in a parable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks' is a plural noun here, glances, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob wrestled with an angel, and to wrestle with God is a figure for earnest, struggling prayer.

clue.text: Pleasure getting tanned is leaving delicate skins

indicators.note: getting a tanning is being beaten, so the letters are knocked about
is shortened to an apostrophe-s; its leaving takes one letter away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sunbathing for pleasure leaves delicate skin damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delicate skins' sounds like a sunbather's, but means thin membranes.
explanation.definitionFit: The pleurae are the thin membranes lining the chest and covering the lungs.

clue.text: Occupied with bearing up noosed rope?

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters run from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: at as in engaged in, at work
air is bearing or manner

explanation.surface: Someone busy carrying a looped rope upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A riata is a lariat, a lasso rope ending in a running noose.

clue.text: Fantastic trip out in Yankee chopper, no matter what

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of axe

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful or unreal, so the letters are made over

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild trip out in an American helicopter, whatever it costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' wants to be a helicopter; it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means at any price, that is, whatever the cost.

clue.text: Yah, back round accommodation of a middlingly U sort?

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one piece goes about the other
back means running backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: yah is a posh way of saying yes
a bank accommodation is a loan

explanation.surface: A braying posh voice backing a request for lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: U means upper-class; a Sloane Ranger is an upper-middle-class Londoner from around Sloane Square in Chelsea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloaney describes the manners of a Sloane Ranger, a well-to-do but not aristocratic type.

clue.text: Dark gibe about enemy?

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: a shy is a gibe or sneer, as in having a shy at someone
a wart is a loathed, objectionable person

explanation.surface: A sinister taunt aimed at a foe.
explanation.walkthrough: The gibe splits after its first letter to hold the other word.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarthy describes a dark or dusky complexion, so it is a synonym of dark.

clue.text: Fellow with a way to restrain ruling politician on the left

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a sister is a fellow member
the ins are the party in office
wise is an old word for way or manner, as in in no wise

explanation.surface: A man with a method for curbing a left-wing governing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' looks male but means a fellow member, a sister.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is heraldic and archaic for left, so sinisterwise means towards or on the left.

clue.text: Fine guy to miss hoovering first of rooms is house-trained

indicators.note: hoovering is sucking up, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: well means fine, in good health
a guy is a man
to miss something is to feel the need of it

indicators.note: first of keeps only the opening letter

parts.note: opening letter

explanation.surface: A decent chap who skips vacuuming the rooms is nonetheless domesticated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House-trained' sounds like a pet or a chore-doing husband; it is used figuratively for polite.
explanation.definitionFit: House-trained is used jocularly of people who have learnt good manners, so it means polite.

clue.text: Pips being 75 per cent sour and 50 per cent bad

indicators.note: three quarters of a four-letter word drops one letter

parts.note: acid means sour

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word keeps just two

parts.note: nice once meant wanton or foolish, a bad quality

explanation.surface: Fruit seeds rated by percentages of sourness and badness.
explanation.walkthrough: The obsolete sense of nice, wanton or foolish, makes bad fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Acini are the small seeds or drupelets of a berry such as a grape or raspberry, so pips.

clue.text: Gross post that's officially ordered?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: utter, flagrant, as in gross incompetence
second meaning: a position or grade
third meaning: graded by status, placed in order

explanation.surface: A rude letter that was sent by order of the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two: the adjective, the noun for a position, and the verb in its past sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means flagrant or coarse, a position in a hierarchy, and to arrange by grade.

clue.text: Forgotten vows in the guise of filling these somehow

indicators.note: filling something means going inside it
somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written
as means in the role or guise of

explanation.surface: Wedding vows forgotten while playing a part.
explanation.walkthrough: Forgotten marks an obsolete word: Spenser's heastes are behests or vows.
explanation.definitionFit: Heast is a Spenserian form of hest, a command or vow, now obsolete.

clue.text: Holding tincture Scots lift up bowls

indicators.note: holding means keeping within, so one piece sits inside the other
in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: lift is the Scots word for the sky
or is gold in heraldry, one of the tinctures

explanation.surface: Scotsmen raising medicine-filled bowls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowls' is a cricket verb: to york a batsman is to bowl them with a yorker, a ball pitched at the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To york is to bowl a batsman out with a yorker, so yorks means bowls out.

clue.text: Kiwi munchkin literally facing time to be still

parts.note: lit is the abbreviation for literally
T is the abbreviation for time
to lie is to remain still

explanation.surface: A tiny New Zealand child is told to stand still and face the clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiwi means New Zealand: the answer is NZ slang for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: In New Zealand usage a littlie is a young child, and a munchkin is an informal word for a small child.

clue.text: Eccentricity packing small screen part played by Hitchcock, say

indicators.note: packing means stuffing something inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: camo is short for camouflage, a concealing screen; small signals the shortened form
e is the mathematical symbol for the eccentricity of a conic

explanation.surface: An oddity on a small television screen: Hitchcock's famous walk-on parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small screen' wants to be television, but it is a clipped camouflage screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock famously appeared briefly in his own films; a brief appearance by a well-known figure is a cameo.

clue.text: Mean to go about playing pool — it's never straightforward

indicators.note: going about something is surrounding it, so one word encloses the rest

parts.note: near means stingy or mean
on as in being played or performed
a lin or linn is a pool, especially below a waterfall

explanation.surface: A grumble that pool games never go the simple way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' looks like the game but is a pool of water, a Scots and northern word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nonlinear does not proceed in a straight line or simple sequence, so it is never straightforward.

clue.text: Maori settlements as focus of docusoap

parts.note: ut is Latin for as

indicators.note: the focus of something is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the eight-letter word

explanation.surface: Maori villages being the subject of a reality television series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settlements' looks like villages, but utu is the Maori principle of settling scores or debts by return or recompense.
explanation.definitionFit: Utu in Maori custom means reciprocity or recompense, the settlement of a debt or grievance.

clue.text: Pen pun and a line's done

indicators.note: done means cooked or worked over, so the letters are reprocessed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer's quip: one pun and the line is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like a writing tool, but pen is a Celtic word for a headland, as in Penzance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen in Celtic place names is a headland or promontory, land jutting into the sea.

clue.text: Hard wood with name Calamus

parts.note: the rata is a New Zealand tree with hard red timber
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A botanist names a timber tree with a Latin genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratan, variant spelling of rattan, is the climbing palm of the genus Calamus, whose canes make furniture.

clue.text: Tearing miss about to suffer histrionic simpers

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the other piece
something torn apart has its parts scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
to suffer is an old sense of to let, allow

explanation.surface: A young woman in tears, made to endure theatrical smirking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffer' is the biblical sense, allow, as in 'suffer the little children'.
explanation.definitionFit: A smilet is a little smile in Chambers, so affected, staged simpers fit it.

clue.text: Mean shipmate winding up cranks

indicators.note: winding something up twists it round, so these letters are coiled into a new order

parts.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nasty crewmate teasing the eccentrics on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cranks' looks like odd people, but crank is slang for amphetamine-type drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Crank is street slang for methamphetamine, a stimulant drug of the same family.

clue.text: Stuff up concerning independent radio

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: to cram is to stuff
on means about, concerning
I is the abbreviation for independent

explanation.surface: Someone complaining about an independent radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: Marconi was the Italian pioneer of wireless; his name was once used for radio itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Marconi, after Guglielmo Marconi, was used as a name for wireless telegraphy, radio.

clue.text: Native doctors pack into farm in Provence, say

indicators.note: into places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a mas is a farmhouse in the south of France
a gang is a pack of people

explanation.surface: Local doctors crammed into a Provencal farmhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mganga is an East African traditional healer or witch doctor.

clue.text: Quiet French nut left Jewish community

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
tete is French for head, and nut is slang for head
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A silent French walnut abandoned a Jewish village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' looks edible; it is slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A shtetl, also spelt shtetel, was a small Jewish town or village in Eastern Europe.

clue.text: Style used vaguely from Chaucer's noble mixed dialect

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
y- is the Middle English prefix of past participles, as in Chaucer's yclept
English, a language mixed from many sources

explanation.surface: A style loosely drawn from a nobleman's hybrid speech in Chaucer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the architectural term: Early English is the first phase of English Gothic, and the phrase is also used loosely for any early style.
explanation.definitionFit: Early English names the first Gothic architectural style in England, and is applied vaguely to old styles generally.

clue.text: Ridiculous losing husband in ripped hat

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: torn means ripped

indicators.note: losing means dropping, and husband stands for a single letter to drop

parts.note: rich means ridiculous, as in 'that's rich'

explanation.surface: A ridiculous torn hat after the husband walks off.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn is a three-cornered hat, as worn in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: In Monaco you kiss a gorgeous girl perhaps

parts.note: tu is French for you, spoken in Monaco
to lip is to kiss

explanation.surface: A Monaco romance: you kiss a stunning woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Monaco' signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulip is old slang for a showy, admired person, so a gorgeous girl is one example.

clue.text: Outside broadcast stream shows French item

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for outside broadcast
a jet is a stream of liquid

explanation.surface: A television outside broadcast covers a French news item.
explanation.definitionFit: Objet is French for object, an item, as in objet d'art.

clue.text: Station in Deolali turning over this auld wifie's benefit

indicators.note: turning something over flips it end to end, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a tanna or tana is an Indian police station; Deolali is a town in India

explanation.surface: An old Scotswoman's pension paid from an Indian station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This auld wifie's' marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Annat in Scots law is the half-year's stipend paid to a dead minister's family, a benefit.

clue.text: Cashier's reference possibly clearing second article

indicators.note: clearing means removing, so a letter goes

parts.note: an annual is a yearbook, a possible reference work
the second of the two letters that are indefinite articles

explanation.surface: A bank teller's reference being cleared of an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' is not the bank teller but a verb: to cashier is to dismiss or discard.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier is to discharge or annul, especially an officer's commission.

clue.text: Follower before finding personal prestige

parts.note: a man is a follower or servant
a is short for ante, before

explanation.surface: A disciple ahead of the pack winning personal standing.
explanation.walkthrough: Mana is a Polynesian word for authority and prestige.
explanation.definitionFit: Mana is Maori and Polynesian for authority, influence and standing that a person holds.

clue.text: Personnel handing over odd letters for redundant servant

indicators.note: handing over the odd ones means giving them up, so only the evenly placed letters stay

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A staff department laying off a surplus worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redundant' suggests losing a job, but here it means obsolete: the word is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: An esne was a labourer or slave in Anglo-Saxon England, an archaic word for a servant.

clue.text: Judge, pretty much firm at first, backing a Greek island council

indicators.note: pretty much means almost all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: firm as in staunch, loyal
J is the abbreviation for judge

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: A, GR for Greek, I for island

explanation.surface: A judge, staunch at first, supporting a council on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' places the clipped word ahead of the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A loya jirga is a grand assembly of Afghan tribal leaders, a kind of council.

clue.text: Whole hotel housing old Earl

indicators.note: housing means giving a home to, so one piece is held inside

parts.note: an inn is a hotel
O is the abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: An entire hotel accommodating an elderly aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in one is done all together, as a whole, in a single piece.

clue.text: Showing tone of deep and profound waste?

parts.note: Chambers gives the profound as a noun for the deep, the sea
to blue money is to squander it

explanation.surface: A mournful remark on a deep, profound wastefulness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep' looks like a wordplay piece beside profound, but it belongs to the definition: the colour of the deep.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea blue is the colour of the ocean, the tone the deep shows.

clue.text: Confused about scab being knocked off

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: pied type is jumbled, so pied means confused
a rat or scab is a strikebreaker

explanation.surface: A muddled strikebreaker getting beaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked off' is slang for copied illegally, not beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Knocked-off goods are cheap illicit copies, the same thing as pirated ones.

clue.text: Section corporal split

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for section
a corporal is the linen cloth on an altar, and a pall is a similar altar linen

explanation.surface: A military unit's NCO breaks away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporal' looks like the army rank, but it is the cloth on which the Eucharist is placed.
explanation.definitionFit: To spall is to chip or split, as stone splinters off in flakes.
